Integrating Voice AI and Agents via Agentring: Documentation Overview

Introduction to Agentring Integration

Recent documentation for Agentring outlines methods for connecting AI agents with voice interfaces through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and relays. The system supports bidirectional communication, allowing software agents to contact users by phone or letting users consult their agents during a voice call.

Core Communication Directions

  • Agent to User: Tools like Claude Code, OpenClaw, n8n, or custom scripts can initiate phone messages, wait for replies, or place calls via voice AI.
  • User to Agent: During phone calls, voice AI can interact with configured agents and MCP servers to request assistance.

MCP Server Implementation

Agentring provides both local and HTTP-based MCP server options:

  • Local MCP: The `agentring mcp` command runs an MCP server over standard input/output (stdio), compatible with standard client configurations.
  • Streamable HTTP MCP: The `agentring mcp-http` command serves tools over HTTP at `/mcp`, using bearer tokens for user authentication against a relay.

Configuring Agents

Agents are defined within an `agents.yaml` file, specifying command arguments and parameters. The documentation highlights security considerations, advising users to apply strict allowlists and understand that voice AI acts on spoken inputs.

Verification and Next Steps

To verify configurations, users can inspect documentation files, test local agents via command line utilities, and review implementation recipes provided in the official repository.
